text: If someone hears a public call to testify and, though he is a witness—having seen something or come to know it—does not speak up, he has sinned and must bear his guilt.

versions.text: If someone sins because he hears a public call to testify—and he is a witness, whether he has seen something or come to know it—and he does not speak up, he must bear his guilt.
versions.explanation: "Sins because he hears" wrongly makes the hearing the cause of the sin; in the Hebrew the sin lies in failing to testify after being placed under adjuration. The revised wording also removes the double "and" that breaks the oral rhythm.

versions.text: If someone sins in this way: he hears a public call to testify, and though he is a witness—having seen something or come to know it—he does not speak up, he must bear his guilt.
versions.explanation: The colon after "in this way" creates a structure that is hard to follow when read aloud: the listener hears a colon-list opening but then receives a conditional clause followed by a consequence. Recasting the sentence keeps the Hebrew logic (the sin lies in withholding testimony after adjuration) while giving a single clean conditional that flows in oral reading.

text: Or if someone touches anything unclean—whether the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of an unclean swarming creature—and it escapes his notice, then he is unclean and has incurred guilt.

versions.text: Or if someone touches anything unclean—the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of an unclean swarming creature—and it escapes his notice, he is unclean and has incurred guilt.
versions.explanation: Without a connective, the final clause runs on awkwardly when read aloud; "then" marks the consequence clearly and matches the pattern of verses 3–4.

versions.text: Or if someone touches anything unclean—the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of an unclean swarming creature—and it escapes his notice, then he is unclean and has incurred guilt.
versions.explanation: In Hebrew the list is introduced by "or" and offers examples alongside the general category "anything unclean"; as it stands the bare apposition can be heard as limiting uncleanness to these three carcasses. Adding "whether" preserves the general category and its illustrative examples, and it also smooths the reading aloud.

text: Or if he touches human uncleanness—any uncleanness by which a person becomes unclean—and it escapes his notice, but afterward he comes to know it, he has incurred guilt.

Or if someone swears rashly with his lips to do harm or to do good—whatever a person may rashly swear in an oath—and it escapes his notice, but afterward he comes to know it, he has incurred guilt in any of these ways.
When he becomes guilty in any of these ways, he shall confess the sin he has committed.

As his penalty for the sin he has committed, he shall bring to the LORD a female from the flock, a ewe lamb or a female goat, as a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin.

versions.text: As his penalty for the sin he has committed, he shall bring to the LORD a female from the flock, a lamb or a young goat, as a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew specifies a female lamb (כִּשְׂבָּה) and a female goat (שְׂעִירַת עִזִּים); "a lamb or a young goat" loses the required specification of sex, which is the point of the verse.

text: But if he cannot afford a lamb, he shall bring to the LORD as his penalty for the sin he has committed two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
He shall bring them to the priest, who shall present first the one for the sin offering. He shall wring off its head at the neck without severing it,
and he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering against the side of the altar, while the rest of the blood is drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
The second bird he shall prepare as a burnt offering, according to the regulation. So the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.

But if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring as his offering for the sin he has committed a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall put no oil on it and lay no frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
He shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take a handful of it as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar on top of the offerings made by fire to the LORD. It is a sin offering.
So the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed in any of these ways, and he will be forgiven. The rest shall belong to the priest, as with the grain offering.
The LORD said to Moses:

If someone commits a breach of faith and sins unintentionally against any of the holy things of the LORD, he shall bring to the LORD as his guilt offering a ram without blemish from the flock, valued in silver shekels by the sanctuary shekel, as a guilt offering.

He shall make restitution for the holy thing in which he sinned, adding a fifth to it, and give it to the priest. The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
If someone sins by doing any of the things the LORD has commanded not to be done, even without knowing it, he is guilty and must bear his iniquity.

He shall bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the flock, at the set value, as a guilt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for the error he committed unknowingly, and he will be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering; he has surely incurred guilt before the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses:
If someone sins and commits a breach of faith against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor about something entrusted to him or left in his care, or by robbery, or by defrauding his neighbor,
or if he finds lost property and lies about it and swears falsely—in any of these things that people do and so sin—
then, when he has sinned and become guilty, he shall return what he took by robbery or gained by fraud, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found,
or anything about which he swore falsely. He shall repay it in full and add a fifth to it, giving it to its owner on the day he brings his guilt offering.
And he shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD: a ram without blemish from the flock, at the set value; he shall bring it to the priest.

versions.text: And he shall bring to the LORD his guilt offering: a ram without blemish from the flock, at the set value, brought to the priest as a guilt offering.
versions.explanation: The current rendering repeats "guilt offering" twice in one sentence and the passive "brought to the priest" is clumsy for oral reading; the Hebrew simply directs that the animal be brought to the priest.

text: The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for any of the things he did that brought guilt upon him.
